Active life expectancy from named life-table and prevalence ranges

https://healtheconomics.wiki/ontologies/hemo/HEMO_7006594
Type implementation
has description in the module Person-years for the bands are in a column range named PersonYearsByBand, the dependency prevalence of the same bands in a range of the same size named DependentShareByBand, and the survivors at the starting age in a cell named SurvivorsAtStartAge. The formula, in a cell named ActiveLifeExpectancy, works for any number of bands because SUMPRODUCT evaluates the array 1 minus the prevalence without array entry. A blank prevalence cell is treated as 0, so that band counts as wholly active, and a blank SurvivorsAtStartAge returns #DIV/0!.
has implementation text =SUMPRODUCT(1-DependentShareByBand,PersonYearsByBand)/SurvivorsAtStartAge
has module record identifier HE-IM-ALE-001
has title in the module Active life expectancy from named life-table and prevalence ranges
has title key active-life-expectancy-from-named-life-table-and-prevalence-ranges
implements formula or function Sullivan active life expectancy over three age bands with life expectancy and dependent years
is written in language Excel

excel implementation of HE-CF-ACCS-001

https://healtheconomics.wiki/ontologies/hemo/HEMO_7006623
Type implementation
has description in the module Name a block of m rows and n columns of travel times TravelTimes, a column of m populations PopColumn, a row of n capacities SupplyRow and the threshold ThresholdCF. In a row of n cells named CatchPopRow enter `=SUMPRODUCT((INDEX(TravelTimes,0,COLUMNS($A$1:A$1))<=ThresholdCF)*PopColumn)` and fill right; in a row of n cells named RatioRow enter `=IF(INDEX(CatchPopRow,COLUMNS($A$1:A$1))>0,INDEX(SupplyRow,COLUMNS($A$1:A$1))/INDEX(CatchPopRow,COLUMNS($A$1:A$1)),0)` and fill right. In a column of m cells named AccessColumn enter `=SUMPRODUCT((INDEX(TravelTimes,ROWS($A$1:A1),0)<=ThresholdCF)*RatioRow)` and fill down. A cell named MeanAccessCF holds `=SUMPRODUCT(PopColumn,AccessColumn)/SUM(PopColumn)` and a cell named VarAccessCF holds `=SUMPRODUCT(PopColumn,(AccessColumn-MeanAccessCF)^2)/SUM(PopColumn)`, both in GPs per person; multiply the mean by 10,000 and the variance by 10,000 squared for the article's units. INDEX with a row or column argument of 0 returns a whole column or row, and SUMPRODUCT evaluates the comparisons as arrays without array entry, so the formulas work in every Excel version.
has implementation text =SUMPRODUCT((INDEX(TravelTimes,0,COLUMNS($A$1:A$1))<=ThresholdCF)*PopColumn)
implements formula or function Computational function for two-step floating catchment area scores, mean and spread for any number of sites

No-programme run in B (S), C (I) and E (new infections), programme run in G (S), H (I) and I (new infections), static programme run in K (S) and L (new infections), and the discount factor in M. With T steps in rows 2 to T+1, a cell named `AvertStaticTotal` holds `=SUM(E2:E201)-SUM(L2:L201)` and a cell named `AvertDynamicTotal` holds `=SUM(E2:E201)-SUM(I2:I201)` for 200 steps, and the discounted dynamic cost is `=CostPerInf*SUMPRODUCT(M2:M201,E2:E201-I2:I201)`. has description in the module With one row per group in ranges named GroupShare, HealthOptionA and HealthOptionB, the shares adding to 1, and the bracket ends in cells named BracketLow and BracketHigh, a helper table holds the lower end in column A, the upper end in column B, the midpoint in column C and the difference in column D. Row 2 has `=BracketLow`, `=BracketHigh`, `=(A2+B2)/2` and `=SUMPRODUCT(GroupShare,HealthOptionA^(1-C2))^(1/(1-C2))-SUMPRODUCT(GroupShare,HealthOptionB^(1-C2))^(1/(1-C2))`, and row 3 has `=IF(SIGN(D2)=SIGN(DiffAtLow),C2,A2)` and `=IF(SIGN(D2)=SIGN(DiffAtLow),B2,C2)` in columns A and B with the formulas of columns C and D copied down from row 2, where DiffAtLow holds the same difference at BracketLow. Row 3 is then copied down to row 41, and after these 40 rows the last midpoint, held in CritEpsilon, is within about 1E-10 of the root for a bracket 30 wide. The table has no geometric-mean branch, so a midpoint of exactly 1 would return #DIV/0!, which never happens with bracket ends 0 and 30. The table uses classic functions only.
has implementation text =BracketLow

has description in the module On the sheet of HE-IM-IPH-001, with a column range named MustFund (D2 to D5) holding 1 for each required programme and 0 otherwise, enter `=MMULT(E2:H2,MustFund)` in L2 for the number of required programmes in the package and `=(I2<=Budget)*(L2=SUM(MustFund))*J2` in M2, and fill both down to row 17. Then `=MAX(M2:M17)` in a cell named ForcedOptimum gives the best total with the requirement, `=MATCH(ForcedOptimum,M2:M17,0)` in BestPackageRow gives the row of PackageMatrix that holds the package, the first such row when packages tie, and `=IntegerOptimum-ForcedOptimum` in EquityRuleCost gives the QALYs forgone. MustFund needs a 0 typed for each programme not required, since MMULT returns #VALUE! when a cell is blank. When the required programmes cost more than Budget no package qualifies, and the sheet then gives a ForcedOptimum of 0, a BestPackageRow of 1 (the empty package) and an EquityRuleCost equal to IntegerOptimum, so a ForcedOptimum of 0 with a programme required reads as no qualifying package. For more than four programmes PackageMatrix needs 2^n rows and n columns.
has implementation text =MMULT(E2:H2,MustFund)

has description in the module With the four programmes' costs in a column range named ProgCosts (B2 to B5), their QALY gains in ProgQALYs (C2 to C5) and the budget in Budget, the first formula, entered in E2 and filled to H17, builds a range named PackageMatrix whose row k holds the binary digits of k less 1, one column per programme, so its 16 rows are every package. In each row I2 holds the package cost, J2 its QALYs and K2 its QALYs when it fits and zero when it does not, each filled down to row 17, and the cell named IntegerOptimum takes the largest value in K2 to K17. With the health of the league table of whole programmes (WholeHealth of HE-IM-CELT-003, extended to four rows) in RuleHealth and the divisible fill of HE-CF-CELT-001 in DivisibleHealth, the last two formulas return the cells named GainOverRule and IndivisibilityLoss. MMULT of a one-row package and a four-row column of costs or QALYs is a single value, so it needs no array entry in an ordinary cell. MMULT returns #VALUE! when any cell of ProgCosts or ProgQALYs is blank or holds text, so every programme needs a number in both ranges.
has implementation text =MOD(INT((ROW()-ROW($E$2))/2^(COLUMN()-COLUMN($E$2))),2); =MMULT(E2:H2,ProgCosts); =MMULT(E2:H2,ProgQALYs); =(I2<=Budget)*J2; =MAX(K2:K17); =IntegerOptimum-RuleHealth; =DivisibleHealth-IntegerOptimum

has description in the module `psa_run <- function(N, mu, s, rho, q, dC, lambda, seed) { set.seed(seed); S <- matrix(c(s[1]^2, rho*s[1]*s[2], rho*s[1]*s[2], s[2]^2), 2); L <- t(chol(S)); Z <- matrix(rnorm(2*N), 2); B <- mu + L %*% Z; INHB <- q*(exp(-B[1, ]-B[2, ])-exp(-B[1, ]))-dC/lambda; c(ENHB = mean(INHB), P_CE = mean(INHB > 0), EL_new = mean(pmax(-INHB, 0)), EL_comp = mean(pmax(INHB, 0)), MCSE = sd(INHB)/sqrt(N), r = cor(B[1, ], B[2, ])) }` Run as `psa_run(10000, c(log(0.25), log(0.8)), c(0.1, 0.2), -0.5, 0.5, 15000, 25000, 2026)`, which returns an expected incremental net health benefit of about minus 0.0761 QALYs, a probability of 0.4136, expected losses of about 0.2342 and 0.1581, a Monte Carlo standard error of about 0.0049 and a sample correlation of about minus 0.5005. https://healtheconomics.wiki/ontologies/hemo/HEMO_7006563
Type implementation
has description in the module With the GPs in cells named GPsPracticeX and GPsPracticeY, the populations in PopNbhdA, PopNbhdB and PopNbhdC, the travel times in TimeAtoX, TimeAtoY, TimeBtoX, TimeBtoY, TimeCtoX and TimeCtoY and the threshold in ThresholdMinutes, the five formulas return the supply ratios in cells named RatioPracticeX and RatioPracticeY and the scores in AccessNbhdA, AccessNbhdB and AccessNbhdC, in GPs per person; multiplying by 10,000 gives the article's units. Excel treats TRUE as 1 and FALSE as 0 in multiplication, so each comparison works as the catchment indicator. For the article's inputs they return 0.000266667, 0.000153846, 0.000266667, 0.000420513 and 0.000153846. A blank travel-time cell counts as 0 minutes in the comparison and so places that neighbourhood inside the catchment; with TimeCtoX blank, C joins X's catchment and B's score falls from 4.205 to 3.761 per 10,000 (checked in Excel).
has implementation text =GPsPracticeX/((TimeAtoX<=ThresholdMinutes)*PopNbhdA+(TimeBtoX<=ThresholdMinutes)*PopNbhdB+(TimeCtoX<=ThresholdMinutes)*PopNbhdC); =GPsPracticeY/((TimeAtoY<=ThresholdMinutes)*PopNbhdA+(TimeBtoY<=ThresholdMinutes)*PopNbhdB+(TimeCtoY<=ThresholdMinutes)*PopNbhdC); =(TimeAtoX<=ThresholdMinutes)*RatioPracticeX+(TimeAtoY<=ThresholdMinutes)*RatioPracticeY; =(TimeBtoX<=ThresholdMinutes)*RatioPracticeX+(TimeBtoY<=ThresholdMinutes)*RatioPracticeY; =(TimeCtoX<=ThresholdMinutes)*RatioPracticeX+(TimeCtoY<=ThresholdMinutes)*RatioPracticeY
